decisions.reason: The paper does not state a single overall replication verdict covering the study as a whole, instead evaluating three replicated experiments (Figures 2, 3D, and 5 of Ward et al., 2010) and their meta-analyses individually. The shipped quote ('To summarize, for this experiment we found results that were in the same direction as the original study and statistically significant where predicted.') only summarizes the first two experiments (lines 299 and 390). In the third experiment (AML patient samples, replicating Figure 5), the authors explicitly qualify their conclusion because the planned confirmatory comparison on IDH1-mutant samples using total ion chromatograms (TIC) was not statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (p = 0.063) and showed nonsignificant meta-analytic pooling (p = 0.114) with significant heterogeneity (Cochran's Q p = 0.031). Under Rule 2 of the codebook, because the authors present their replication comparisons as partly supporting the original findings and partly failing to reach predicted statistical significance on a planned comparison, the outcome is 'mixed'.
